tensions: Primary tension is no longer a position, it is behavior. The rulebook's 7-day minimum hold was written on September 22 to stop fee drag, and it was broken three times in the nine days after: SUI held 2.5 hours, QNT held 22 hours, NEAR flipped in 8 hours, net -$20.96 plus fees. Total explicit fees since September 20 are $23.57 over 21 orders, 1.9% of lifetime deposits in eleven days, and the taker rate has worsened from 0.75% to 0.95%. The system's edge this cycle came from the two patient decisions (W held eight days for +19.2%, ARB sold ahead of its October 16 unlock) and was partly given back by the impatient ones. Second tension: Fear and Greed reads 74 (Greed) while total market cap fell 2.9% in 24 hours and eight of nine positions are green. Sentiment is lagging price, and that order usually resolves downward. Yet dominance is falling and the Altcoin Season Index has nearly tripled in a month to 61, which argues the alt leg is mid-move, not done. Those two point opposite ways and only the sentiment one has a timer. Third tension: dry powder is $1.41, confirmed by a rejected order preview, so the fee gate rather than the thesis now decides every allocation. At a 3-4% round trip, the bar for any rotation is high enough that the default is paralysis — which is correct when nothing is broken, and dangerous the day something is. UNRESOLVED DATA ISSUES, needs James: (1) AVAX, 9.0511 units at a $99.00 basis, has NO order history in Robinhood under any date — origin unexplained, and its entry date is therefore unknown, which means its 7-day hold eligibility cannot be verified. (2) Lifetime deposits are ambiguous: the scan config says $1,231 but two of seven history rows said $1,331, which is why yesterday's return read +48.4% and today's reads +60.5%. I normalized the series to $1,231 per the config; if $1,331 is correct, every return figure on this board is overstated by about 12 points.

opening.text: Nine positions, nine holds, and buying power is $1.41 — I pre-flighted a $150 AAVE buy and Robinhood rejected it outright for insufficient funds. That is the whole scan in one line: every buy from here is a forced sale of something healthy. Worst position is ZEC at -6.5% against a -15% stop. Nothing is thesis-broken, nothing is 21-day dead money, nothing breaches the 25% weight cap (LINK is highest at 21.1%). A no-trade day is a decision.

The tradable idea I modeled was AAVE, +18.6% over 7 days and +31.8% over 30, funded by trimming ZEC. I killed it on arithmetic. Robinhood's taker fee just moved from 0.75% to 0.95%, so a round trip is now ~1.9% in explicit fees plus 1-2% of spread — call it 3-4%. The v5.7.22 gate wants more than 3% of net forward edge. Paying 4% to chase a name already up 32% in a month, with Fear and Greed at 74, is not a 4% edge. PASS.

The honest finding this morning is not in the book, it is in the blotter. v5.7.22 imposed a 7-day minimum hold on September 22 specifically to stop fee drag. In the nine days since: SUI held 2.5 hours for -$6.82, QNT held 22 hours for -$20.97, NEAR flipped in 8 hours for +$6.83. Net -$20.96 on trades the rules forbade. Explicit fees since September 20 are $23.57 across 21 orders — 1.9% of all capital ever deposited, burned in eleven days. The two things that actually made money were W, held eight days for +19.2%, and dodging the October 16 ARB unlock. Both were patience, not activity.

Regime says stay in alts and stop looking at BTC. Dominance is 58.6% and FALLING, down 1.11%, while the Altcoin Season Index has gone from 23 to 61 in a month. Step 1b needs dominance above 58 AND rising AND Bitcoin beating the median alt; it is above 58 and fails the other two, so the BTC/ETH rotation does not fire. Derivatives are clean — funding runs +4% to +11% annualized with no froth, and NEAR funding is actually negative at -2% despite +143% over 30 days, meaning shorts are paying us. No unlock touches the book: October's supply events are ENA, 2Z, SUI, ARB, EIGEN and WLD, and we are already out of SUI and ARB. ZEC shipped Ironwood, a formally verified pool replacing Orchard, so the privacy thesis is intact and the -7.7% week is a pullback off +61%, not a break.
